look: Chalk geometry: a dark maths-explainer look (3Blue1Brown-style): clean vector dots, arrows and grids drawn in glowing strokes on a dark ground, shapes morphing smoothly, short serif captions

scenes.name: 11a No ground truth
scenes.desc: Big dots in a straight row and a mesh line with a hole and a part with no dots.

scenes.name: 11b Accuracy
scenes.desc: Sample points on the mesh, lines to the nearest dot; long lines where no dots are.

scenes.name: 11c Completeness
scenes.desc: Lines from every dot to the closest point on the mesh; long lines over the hole.

scenes.name: 11d Why both
scenes.desc: A tiny mesh and an overlong mesh each pass one test and fail the other.

scenes.name: 11e Chamfer
scenes.desc: Lines become bars, each list gets its average, Chamfer is the average of the two.

scenes.name: 11f Scale
scenes.desc: The figure grows and shrinks; raw numbers change but the percentage of the diagonal stays.

scenes.name: 11g Threshold
scenes.desc: Choose tau; short lines turn blue, long lines stay yellow.

scenes.name: 11h F-score
scenes.desc: Ticks and crosses count precision, then recall, then the F formula.

scenes.name: 11i Why F
scenes.desc: A table shows plain averages versus F for three meshes.

scenes.name: 11j Our numbers
scenes.desc: The four Poisson runs with Chamfer, F at 1% and F at 0.5%.

scenes.name: 11k Smooth or crumpled
scenes.desc: A smooth and a zig-zag mesh over the same dots; their arrows agree or disagree with the dots' arrows.

scenes.name: 11l Colours
scenes.desc: Dot colours against texture colours, then the real point-colour and photo textures with their scores.

scenes.name: 11m Watertight
scenes.desc: Water poured into a closed shape and a shape with a hole; open ends marked; printable methods listed.

scenes.name: 11n At a glance
scenes.desc: A summary card of every score, its question and what it catches.
